So, this is a rather naive and misguided
attempt to try to jin up mark of the
beast vibes in order to play on
Christian anxieties about the Antichrist
and the end times. And it is naive and
misguided for two main reasons, but
there are many others. The first main
reason is that what's going on in this
video that is more than 2 years old has
absolutely nothing whatsoever to do with
what is described in Revelation 13
16 and 17 as the mark of the beast.
Because what is described there is a
karagma, a brand, a stamp, a mark that
is etched, branded, carved into either
the right hand or the forehead. And
what's going on in this video is what's
called Amazon 1, which is just a scanner
that scans the unique pattern of veins
under the skin of your palm. And so
you're not receiving, as the text of
Revelation says, any kind of mark
whatsoever. It's just scanning either
your right or your left hand to
determine what your vein palm
fingerprint is to tell if that's really
you. So, it's just a means of
identification that uses your right or
your left hand exactly as it already
exists. There is no mark to receive. So,
this is not what is being described in
Revelation 13. That's the first main
reason this is naive and misguided. The
second main reason is that there is no
mark of the beast on the way because
Revelation 13 is not a prophecy about
the future. It was late 1st century CE
apocalyptic literature and imagery
intended to evoke an emotional response
in early followers of Jesus and exhort
them to greater faithfulness to their
community and to keep them unspotted
from the evil Roman Empire. And the mark
of the beast is intended to appeal to
imagery associated with the Roman
Empire. And there are three different
main ways that it does this. The idea
that it is something on the right hand
or the forehead will evoke a sense of
counterfeit worship practices. Because
in all the Bible and in early Judaism,
there's only one thing that associates
the hand and the forehead and that is
the notion that you should have the law
on your hand and and your forehead. And
that results in the practice of
felactories. And so there was a worship
practice developing in the first century
CE within Judaism related to putting
certain texts of the Torah on little
pieces of paper and rolling them up
tight and placing them in boxes that go
on the front and the back of the
forehead and have a leather strap that
goes around the left hand. And so the
association of the right hand and the
forehead evokes this idea of a
counterfeit worship practice that would
be associated with Rome. Now, another
thing it evokes is the notion of a mark
on the forehead, which was a way to
identify people who belonged to an
enslaver or a deity. And you can see
this in the book of Ezekiel. There's a
chapter where God says to go through
Jerusalem and mark everyone on the
forehead who is outraged about the
wickedness and the iniquity that is
running rampant in Jerusalem. And then
God sends executioners through the city
and they are to execute anyone and
everyone who does not have the mark on
the forehead because the mark is a way
to identify who is a follower of God who
belongs to God. And so it's also evoking
that notion of fidelity to a specific
deity. Are you a follower of the God of
Israel or are you a follower of the
imperial deity? So that's also being
evoked in the concept of the mark of the
beast. And then the idea that you cannot
buy or sell without the mark evokes the
idea of Roman coinage which carries the
face or the mark and the name of the
emperor and that is something that would
be exchanged with the right hand and you
could not buy or sell in the Roman
Empire without that mark. So those are
the three main ideas that are being
evoked by this imagery of the mark of
the beast and it is entirely confined to
the late 1st century CE. The book of
revelation is not about today. It is not
about any point in our future. There is
no mark of the beast to look out for.
Nobody needs to be anxious about any of
that. We can put that behind us and we
can grow the hell up and get on with
trying to make the world a better place
for everybody. And the fit for this
